Been using pfsense for years with very little trouble. Occasionally it has issues with auto-upgrade, so I swapped over from physical hardware a while back to hosting it inside my virtual farm -- so now I can snapshot the thing before doing an upgrade. Having it in a VM host also gives you the ability to generate a bunch of virtual networks for, say, DMZs and such, so if you do have a breach, it's fully contained in a non-existent network. Needless to say, I highly suggest this setup if you can put the hardware together for it.

Also of note is that pfsense was forked over to opnsense some time ago, if you're interested in a more open development process. I haven't tried this one out, so can't speak to it, but I've heard good things.
